name: Sandals
overview: Scripture uses sandals and shoes as significant symbols reflecting holiness, readiness, and covenant. In Exodus and Joshua, removing shoes signifies encountering holy ground, underscoring reverence before God. Wearing shoes during the Passover meal illustrates preparedness and urgency in obeying the Lord’s command. Additionally, the act of removing a shoe in Ruth serves as a tangible testimony in confirming agreements, highlighting the cultural and spiritual weight sandals held in Israel’s life and worship.
